notes: Cards to merge into events_prologue.json's events list. New things the loader must learn: type 'news' (a headline in the Signals or news list, no pause, no choice; its single 'Noted' choice is for the schema only); trigger predicates pool_open, cold_storage, club_member, pps, cash_below_reserve, 'fixed:<quarter> if <predicate>' and 'trigger:<predicate>'; effect keys pool{...}, club{...} and sell_scrypt_gpus. Existing effect keys (cash, flag, bandwidth_next, duration_quarters) keep their meaning.

events.title: A Coin for GPUs
events.body: A new coin called Litecoin goes live. It uses scrypt, a puzzle meant to suit ordinary CPUs and GPUs rather than the FPGA boards bitcoin is moving to. Your GPU can mine it from today.

choices.label: Point a GPU at it (Rig screen)

events.real_basis: Litecoin client 0.1.0 released 7 Oct 2011, network live 13 Oct 2011 [B/C]

events.title: Pools Under Fire
events.body: Pools across the forums report floods of junk traffic. The biggest pools are hit most often.
events.real_basis: Pools were the main DDoS target in the second half of 2011 (Vasek, Thornton, Moore, FC 2014) [A]

events.title: A Hosting Breach
events.body: A hosting provider is breached and a well-known pool loses 3,094 BTC from its hot wallet. Its operator covers the loss himself.

events.title: The Chain Splits
events.body: A software upgrade splits the bitcoin chain for a few hours. Several pools lose block rewards before it is patched.

events.title: A Payout Script Hijacked
events.body: A mid-size pool's payout script is hijacked and 923 BTC goes out. A web wallet freezes 569 of it and sends it back.

events.title: Silver Doubles
events.body: Litecoin nearly doubles in a day. Every forum thread asks which Radeon to buy.

events.title: A Joke Coin
events.body: A coin with a Shiba Inu logo launches. Its block rewards are random, up to a million coins a block. It also runs on scrypt.

events.title: Radeons Sell Out
events.body: High-end Radeons sell out. Some go for over $700, well above list.

events.title: Scrypt ASICs, Pay Now
events.body: The first scrypt ASIC pre-orders open. Pay now, ship later. GPU miners do the arithmetic.

events.title: Dogecoin Fixes Its Reward
events.body: Dogecoin forks at block 145,000: a fixed 250,000 reward and difficulty that adjusts every block. Hopping onto lucky blocks stops paying.

events.title: A Dog on the Track
events.body: A car wrapped in a cartoon dog races at Talladega, paid for with 67.8 million tipped coins.

events.title: The Boxes Ship
events.body: Scrypt ASIC boxes start shipping and the Litecoin network passes 1 TH/s. A GPU that earned dollars a day last winter earns cents. Used GPUs still sell, for now.

choices.label: Sell every GPU on scrypt at the used price

events.real_basis: Shipping from early Sep 2014; 1 TH/s on 15 Sep 2014 [B]

events.title: Two Coins for One
events.body: Dogecoin passes block 371,337. Litecoin mining now earns Dogecoin too, for the same work.

events.title: An Exchange Goes Dark
events.body: A Dogecoin exchange declares bankruptcy and its sister exchange goes dark. About 3,700 BTC is missing. Your coins are in your own wallet.

events.title: Litecoin Halves
events.body: Litecoin block 840,000: the reward falls from 50 to 25.

events.title: Cloud Mining, Charged
events.body: Regulators charge a cloud-mining seller with running a Ponzi scheme. Its virtual miners stopped paying a year ago.
events.real_basis: SEC charges against GAW Miners, 1 Dec 2015 [A]

events.title: Withdrawals Pending
events.body: A big altcoin exchange stops after months of stuck withdrawals. A class action follows.

events.title: Your Pool Is Down
events.body: Halfblock Pool has been flooded with junk traffic since last night. Miners are asking in the thread whether to leave.

choices.label: Buy DDoS protection (from next quarter; 1 Bandwidth)

events.title: The Hot Wallet Is Empty
events.body: Someone got into the server overnight. The pool's payout wallet is empty and miners are owed a week of earnings.

choices.label: Pay the miners from your own cash
Pay what is left and explain

events.real_basis: Pool hot-wallet thefts of 3,094 BTC (Mar 2012) and 923 BTC (Apr 2013); the first operator repaid from his own funds [B]

events.title: A Run of Bad Luck
events.body: Under PPS you pay every share, block or no block. The pool has found few blocks for weeks and your cash is thinning.

choices.label: Switch to PPLNS (1 Bandwidth next quarter)

events.real_basis: PPS shifts variance to the operator (custody.json payout_methods)

events.title: Miners on the Move
events.body: One pool came close to half of all bitcoin mining. Miners are spreading out to smaller pools, and some are asking about yours.

choices.label: Cut the fee to 0% for two quarters

events.real_basis: GHash.IO briefly above 50% of network hashrate, 12-13 Jun 2014 (custody.json note) [B]

events.title: An Offer for the Pool
events.body: The operator of CopperHash wants to fold your miners into his pool. He offers cash for the pool, the domain and the user list.
events.real_basis: Invented; no sourced small-pool sale found (doc 53)

events.title: Three Friends and a Spreadsheet
events.body: Mara, Teo and Jun want in on the ASIC group buy everyone is talking about. Teo brings his two Radeons. Jun has a spreadsheet. They want you, because you have actually mined before.

choices.label: Join (1 Bandwidth; choose your stake, who holds the keys and where it runs)

events.real_basis: Forum group buys of early ASICs, 2012-2013 (preorders.json group_buy) [B]; the friends are invented

events.title: Who Pays the Power?
events.body: The power bill for the club's machines has doubled. Jun wants every machine metered. Mara says that is how friendships end.

events.title: Teo Wants Out
events.body: Bitcoin is over $1,000. Teo wants his share in cash before it falls.

choices.label: Buy his share at market value
Let him sell his share of the coins

events.real_basis: December 2013 peak (events_prologue.json peak_and_silk_road) [B]; Teo is invented

events.title: Someone Wants the Radeons
events.body: A forum buyer offers one and a half times what Teo's cards cost. Scrypt ASIC pre-orders are open.
events.real_basis: GPU prices peaked in early 2014 ($900 against a $550 launch, 4 Mar 2014) [B]

events.title: A Box for the Club
events.body: Jun wants the club to put money into a share of a $9,995 scrypt box from ScryptBox Ltd, shipping 'next quarter'.

choices.label: Buy a quarter share for the club

events.real_basis: Scrypt box pre-orders at $9,995 in Mar 2014, shipping Sep 2014 [B]; vendor invented

events.title: Daily Payouts, Guaranteed
events.body: Jun's cousin bought cloud mining contracts that pay out every day. No machines, no power bill. He wants the club to buy in.
events.real_basis: Cloud-mining Hashlets sold from Aug 2014; payouts fell below fees by Nov 2014; shut Jan 2015; SEC charges Dec 2015 [A]; the seller is invented

events.title: The Spreadsheet Has to Close
events.body: The GPUs earn pennies. Mara wants to sell, Teo wants to keep going, and Jun wants the spreadsheet settled.

choices.label: Keep the club going to the end
